searchText: this can be done socially already without any consensus changes just have miners agree on it I believe it will be harder to do post merge. At least with big mining pools the pool operators paid attention. I keep seeing messages from small validators who haven't updated clients since genesis. then it seems there won't be much social consensus in favor of it, and it would be wrong to enact a change like that that would take away some of the agency of validators Does anyone know if Ethereum provides an ability to do crowdloans via on chain governance similar to Polkadot or if this part of the roadmap? (for reference: https://wiki.polkadot.network/docs/learn-crowdloans ) I do like this capability and haven’t yet seen something similar for Ethereum. no it doesn't. there is not slot auction model like this in Ethereum, L2s compete for settlement on a per block basis Hi, I have read this on internet "As a result, participants with the highest stakes could find it difficult to get validation rewards constantly. So, it offers a credible approach for sharing the wealth." Does it mean that those who have more stake of ETH will be rewarded less compared to those who have less amount of ETH in stacking? No, as with almost all things in the world, percentages are equal (and a certain limited amount of economies of scale applies as well)

excerpts.content:
Hi, I have read this on internet

"As a result, participants with the highest stakes could find it difficult to get validation rewards constantly. So, it offers a credible approach for sharing the wealth."

Does it mean that those who have more stake of ETH will be rewarded less compared to those who have less amount of ETH in stacking?
